name: Shaped window over a fixed world
look: One full-bleed photograph of the client's site stays still behind a shutter painted in the page's ground. Two tall windows cut in it, level and side by side, show the site through a mullion under the title; the scroll widens them outward, closes the bar into one window, holds a beat, then scales the shutter past the screen's edges so the reader pushes through into the place; a flat band of the ground rises across the foot carrying the chapter's one word, then its lede and the action. The shutter is five flat pieces moved by transform: no mask edge, no hairline, no word on the photograph.
reduced: The title, the photograph, the word, the lede and the action under it.

needs.photo: one wide photograph of the client's own site or world (a plant, a test range, a fleet at sea, a game's world)
needs.words: a title of 3-7 words, one word of 6-12 letters, a lede of 18-32 words and one action

never: a software page whose product is a screen (the hero shows the product); a local-business or place page; two different pictures in the two windows; a word of fewer than 4 letters. Never the page's hero: its rest composition is two screens tall (restH 2), so on a phone, under reduced motion and without script the hero would be two screens; it comes below the hero, in a statement slot.
